analysis: Two changes examined. (1) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head line 82 adds `await checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue()` to the periodic capacityRefreshTick. The implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so its behavior (model reload/recovery, download, weight-hash verification, interaction with advertised models and T-012/T-027 weight integrity) cannot be assessed. It runs on the existing actor-isolated tick, and nothing visible shows it bypasses load admission or attestation. (2) ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift head lines 100-125 change drain handling. If lifecycleRemaining==0 and no registered coordinator connection exists, the code waits up to 10s (drainReconnectGrace) for a reconnect, then acknowledges the drain if connected. Otherwise `sessionDown` is set and the drain is reported `.drained`, which previously gave `.timedOut`. Security reasoning: sessionDown requires lifecycleRemaining==0, so no accepted work is outstanding, and nativeOwnersDrained must also be true. A disconnect cancels accepted work per the code comment, and the drain does not release the App Attest worker early, since stopAppAttestWorkerAndWait still gates the outcome. The outcome is stricter-or-equal on isolation: the provider is already disconnected, so no consumer plaintext remains in flight, and the lifecycle barrier cannot weaken A-001 confidentiality. An adversarial coordinator/network could force the disconnect to make a drain complete without an ack. That is an availability/lifecycle-semantics matter and the effect is only a graceful stop/update/logout proceeding, not data exposure. One residual question: logout and update flows that rely on `.drained` as proof the coordinator saw all terminal/usage messages (billing/usage accounting, T-053 revocation ordering) now may proceed without coordinator acknowledgement. The code comment says nothing is buffered after disconnect, so no message is lost beyond what already happened. Callers of hasRegisteredConnection and acknowledgeDrain were not supplied. Next pass should confirm checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue and that hasRegisteredConnection reflects a registered, not merely open, socket.
